craft_claim: Future-self imagery links self-concept to motivation, but it changes behaviour only when joined to plausible, concrete strategies and a reframed meaning of difficulty.

supporting_evidence.note: Possible selves are future-projected elements of self-knowledge, both hoped-for and feared, that provide the cognitive link between self-concept and motivation.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 91(1):188-204, intervention and mediation analyses
supporting_evidence.note: A randomized school intervention showed possible selves alone were insufficient; academic gains required linking possible selves with plausible strategies, congruent identity, and a reframed meaning of difficulty, with effects sustained at two-year follow-up and mediated by change in possible selves.
Marti pairs a forward continental ideal with named obstacles (imported doctrine, internal division), a balanced-vision structure consistent with possible-selves theory.

counterevidence.note: Section B defines possible selves as both hoped-for and feared, and the link from self-concept to motivation runs through the feared future self as well, so future-self imagery is not inherently uplifting and the inspirational use selects one half of a two-sided construct.

scope: Uplift aimed at identity or behavioural change across essay, speech, and blog forms.
exceptions: Purely commemorative or celebratory passages may invoke a future self without a strategy and still function as tone-warm or tone-reverent rather than motivational.
